The [iNaturalist Network](https://www.naturalista.uy/sites/network) is a localised experience that is fully connected to the global iNaturalist community. Network members are local institutions that promote local use and facilitate the use of data from iNaturalist to benefit local 

The aim of this report is to give an account of the importance of the iNaturalist network members by analysing the number of records for each country.

## iNaturalist National Sites

```{r}
#| label: inat-sites
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: 'Members of the iNaturalist Network. Shown in green are the sites from Latin America'

inat_network <- read_csv('data/inat_nodes.csv')

inat_network %>% 
  mutate('#'= row_number()) %>% relocate('#') %>% 
  rename(`Country` = node_country,
         `Node name` = node_name,
         `ID`= node_id,
         `Type`=node_type,
         `Year established` = node_year) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=1) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(row = c(1,4,7,8,10,11,12,17,21), bold = T, color = "white", background = "#228A22")
```

![](https://static.inaturalist.org/wiki_page_attachments/3354-original.png)

```{r}
#| label: temporal-plot
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-height: 4

ggplot(inat_network, aes(x = node_year, 
                         y = 0,          
                         label = node_country)) +
  geom_point(aes(col = node_type), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c('black', '#228a22', '#74AC00', '#b2b2b2ff')) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2013, 2022, 1)) +
  geom_label_repel(
    aes(colour = node_type),
    min.segment.length = 0.1,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    direction = "y",          
    nudge_y = 0.5,            
    segment.size = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('black', '#228a22', '#74AC00', '#b2b2b2ff')) +
  labs(x = '', y = '', col = '') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean() +
  theme(
    legend.position = 'bottom',
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank()   
  )
```

## Methods

We tested different explanatory variables and saw which is the model that best explains the values a country has for iNaturalist. Indicators per country were extracted using the WDI: World Development Indicators (World Bank) on the **20th of March, 2026**. 

**Response variables** (per country):  

  - `n_records`: total number of records on iNaturalist.  
  - `n_users`: number of users recording (this is not exactly the users *from* the country, but users that have generated records in the country).  
  - `n_species`: number of species recorded (this is not necessarily at the species level).
  - `n_projects`: number of projects created.
  - `p_research_grade`: proportion of records from iNaturalist that are "Research Grade" (proxy for quality).  
  - `n_literature`: number of peer-reviewed publications in GBIF using iNat data.  

**Explanatory variables**:  

  - `population`: population of the country (*SP.POP.TOTL*).  
  - `area`: area of the country in km^2^ (*AG.SRF.TOTL.K2*).  
  - `gdp_per_capita`: GDP per capita in US dollars (*NY.GDP.PCAP.CD*).  
  - `gdp_in_research`: % of the GDP of the country dedicated to research *GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS*).  
  - `latitude`: country's centroid latitude (as a proxy of expected biodiversity) (using `rnaturalearth` country polygons).  
  - `iucn_species`: number of species reported for the country on IUCN (using `rnaturalearth` country polygons).  
  - `has_node`: whether a country has a node on the iNaturalist network.   
  - `neighbour_has_node`: whether a country has a neighbouring country that has a node on the iNaturalist network (using `rnaturalearth` country polygons).  

### Data 

We downloaded the data following

```{r}
#| label: variables
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

data_variables <- read_csv('data/data_global_variables.csv')
```

## Summary of the data


```{r}
#| label: time-series
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 10

data_temporal_records_network <- readRDS('data/data_global_time_series.csv')
data_temporal_records_network <- left_join(data_variables, data_temporal_records_network) %>% 
  mutate(has_node = ifelse(!is.na(node_name), 1, 0))

# split data into highlighted and background
highlighted <- data_temporal_records_network %>%
  filter(country_name %in% inat_network$node_country)

node_years <- highlighted %>%
  distinct(country_name, node_year)

highlighted %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n_records_inat, colour = country_name)) +
  # grey background lines (all countries, in every facet)
  geom_line(
    data = data_temporal_records_network %>% rename(country_name2 = country_name),
    aes(group = country_name2),
    colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(colour = "#74AC00", linewidth = 1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(colour = "#74AC00", size = 1.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(
    data = node_years,
    aes(xintercept = node_year),
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey30",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  facet_wrap(~ country_name, ncol = 7) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Number of records (log scale)") +
  ggpubr::theme_cleveland()

```


```{r}
#| label: summary-data
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8

summary_data <- data_variables %>% 
  mutate(is_network =
           case_when(!is.na(node_name) ~ 'Network',
                     country_name == 'United States' ~ 'United States',
                     .default = 'Rest of the world')) %>%
  relocate(is_network) %>%
  group_by(is_network) %>% 
  summarise(n_records = sum(n_records), 
            n_users = sum(n_users), 
            n_species = sum(n_species), 
            n_projects = sum(n_projects), 
            n_literature = sum(n_literature), 
            p_research_grade_mean = round(mean(p_research_grade),3),
            p_research_grade_sd = round(sd(p_research_grade),3))

summary_data %>%
  mutate(perc_records = round(n_records*100/sum(n_records),1), .after = n_records) %>%
  mutate(perc_users = round(n_users*100/sum(n_users),1), .after = n_users) %>%
  mutate(perc_species = round(n_species*100/sum(n_species),1), .after = n_species) %>%
  mutate(perc_projects = round(n_projects*100/sum(n_projects),1), .after = n_projects) %>%
  mutate(perc_literature = round(n_literature*100/sum(n_literature),1), .after = n_literature) %>%
  janitor::adorn_totals('row', ,,, n_records, n_users, n_species, n_projects, n_literature) %>%
  kableExtra::kbl(col.names = c('Network', 'Observations', '(%)',
                                'Users', '(%)',
                                'Species', '(%)',
                                'Projects', '(%)',
                                'Publications', '(%)',
                                'Proportion of RG', 'sd'),
                  digits=3, format.args = list(big.mark = ',')) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') 

  
summary_plot_n_records <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=n_records, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = c(m = 1000000))) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Number of records') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

summary_plot_n_users <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=n_users, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = c(m = 1000000))) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Number of users') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

summary_plot_n_species <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=n_species, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = c(m = 1000000)), 
                     limits = c(0,1500000)) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Number of species') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

summary_plot_n_projects <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=n_projects, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = c(m = 1000000)), 
                     limits = c(0,60000)) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Number of projects') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

summary_plot_n_literature <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=n_literature, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = c(m = 1000000)), 
                     limits = c(0,2500)) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Number of publications') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()


summary_plot_p_research_grade_mean <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x=is_network)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y=p_research_grade_mean, fill=is_network),
           stat = 'identity',
           show.legend = F) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#74AC00',  '#b2b2b2ff', 'black')) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1)) +
  labs(x = '', y = 'Proportion of Research Grade records') +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

(summary_plot_n_records + summary_plot_n_users) / (summary_plot_n_species + summary_plot_n_projects) / (summary_plot_n_literature + summary_plot_p_research_grade_mean) 
```

## Summary of the data for the Network members

```{r}
#| label: site-variables
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

data_variables %>% filter(!is.na(node_name)) %>% 
  select(country_name, node_name, 
         n_records, p_research_grade, 
         n_users, n_species, n_projects,n_literature) %>% 
  arrange(country_name, n_records) %>% 
  rename(Country=country_name,
         Node=node_name, 
         `Observations`= n_records,
         `% Research Grade` = p_research_grade,
         `Users`= n_users,
         `Species`= n_species,
         `Projects`= n_projects,
         `Literature`= n_literature) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=3, format.args = list(big.mark = ',')) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') 
```

### Number of records on iNaturalist

```{r}
#| label: n_inat_country
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

ids <- data_variables %>% 
  select(country_name,node_name, n_records) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_records)) %>% 
  with(which(!is.na(node_name)))

data_variables %>% 
  select(country_name,node_name, n_records) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_records)) %>% 
  mutate('#'= row_number()) %>% relocate('#') %>% 
  rename(`Country` = country_name,
         `Node` = node_name,
         `Observations`=n_records) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=4, format.args = list(big.mark = ',')) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') %>% 
  kableExtra::row_spec(ids, bold = T, color = "white", background = "#228A22") %>% 
  kableExtra::scroll_box(height = '600px')
```

## Associations between variables

### Population of the country

```{r}
#| label: population-plot
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: 
#| - 'Number of records on iNaturalist vs Population of the country'
#| - 'Proportion of Research Grade iNat records vs Population of the country'
#| - 'Number of users recording on iNaturalist vs Population of the country'
#| - 'Number of species recorded on iNaturalist vs Population of the country'

## records
ggplot(data_variables %>% mutate(has_node = as.character(has_node)), 
       aes(population/100000, n_records/1000, label = node_name)) +
  geom_point(aes(col=has_node), size=2, show.legend = F) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('black', '#74AC00')) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', colour = 'black') +
  # # geom_abline(lwd = 1.5, linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_label_repel(aes(fill=has_node), 
                   colour = "black", #fontface = "bold",
                   segment.color = 'black',
                   show.legend = F, max.overlaps= Inf) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#F7F7F7', '#74AC00')) +
  labs(x='Population of the country (hundred thousand)',
       y='Number of records on iNaturalist (thousand)') +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  theme_bw()

## records in research_grade
ggplot(data_variables %>% mutate(has_node = as.character(has_node)), 
       aes(population/100000, p_research_grade, label = node_name)) +
  geom_point(aes(col=has_node), size=2, show.legend = F) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('black', '#74AC00')) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', colour = 'black') +
  # geom_abline(lwd = 1.5, linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_label_repel(aes(fill=has_node), 
                   colour = "black", #fontface = "bold",
                   segment.color = 'black',
                   show.legend = F, max.overlaps= Inf) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c('#F7F7F7', '#74AC00')) +
  labs(x='Population of the country (hundred thousand)',
       y='Proportion of iNat records that reach Research Grade') +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  theme_bw()

## users
ggplot(data_variables %>% mutate(has_node = as.character(has_node)), 
       aes(population/100000, n_users, label = node_name)) +
  geom_point(aes(col=has_node), size=2, show.legend = F) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('black', '#74AC00')) +
  geom_smooth(method='lm', col= 'black') +
  # # geom_abline(lwd = 1.5, linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_label_repel(aes(fill=has_node), 
                   colour = "black", #fontface = "bold",
                   segment.color = 'black',
```

## Modelling

```{r}
#| label: data-regressions
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%

data_regressions <- data_variables %>% 
  select(-c(country_name, region, flag, node_name, node_id, node_type, node_year, place_id)) %>% 
  drop_na(area, population, gdp_per_capita, gdp_in_research, latitude, iucn_species) %>% 
  filter(country_code != 'US')

###

data_regressions %>% 
  select(area, population, gdp_per_capita,
         gdp_in_research, latitude, iucn_species, 
         has_node, neighbour_has_node) %>% 
  cor() %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(digits=3, 
                  format.args = list(big.mark = ',')) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') 

data_regressions %>% 
  select(area, population, gdp_per_capita,
         gdp_in_research, latitude, iucn_species, 
         has_node, neighbour_has_node) %>% 
  cor() %>% 
  corrplot::corrplot(method = 'color',
                     diag = FALSE, type = 'lower',
                     order = 'AOE', tl.col = 'grey15') 

data_regressions %>% 
  select(area, population, gdp_per_capita,
         gdp_in_research, latitude, iucn_species) %>% 
  cor() %>% 
  caret::findCorrelation(., cutoff=0.65, names=T)

data_regressions %>% 
  select(area, population, gdp_per_capita,
         gdp_in_research, latitude, iucn_species) %>% pairs()
```

```{r}
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(data_regressions$area), 
             color = "black", linetype = "dashed", lwd=1) +
  labs(x = 'Area (km2)', y = '', 
       subtitle = str_glue('median = {round(median(data_regressions$area, na.rm = T),1)}')) +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

  geom_histogram(fill = '#74ac00', bins = 20, show.legend = F) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = median(data_regressions$gdp_per_capita), 
             color = "black", linetype = "dashed", lwd=1) +
  labs(x = 'GDP per capita', y = '', 
       subtitle = str_glue('median = {round(median(data_regressions$gdp_per_capita, na.rm = T),1)}')) +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean()

  labs(x = '% of GDP in research', y = '',

plot_hist_latitude <- ggplot(data_regressions, aes(x = latitude)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = '#74ac00', bins = 20, show.legend = F) +
```

## Random forest

### Standardise predictors and outcomes

First log transform (`log10`) and then scale (mean zero).

```{r}
#| label: standr-outcomes
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

data_regressions <- data_regressions %>% 
  mutate(n_records = scale(log10(n_records))[,1]) %>% 
  mutate(n_users = scale(log10(n_users))[,1]) %>% 
  mutate(n_species = scale(log10(n_species))[,1]) %>% 
  mutate(n_projects = scale(log10(n_projects))[,1]) %>% 
  mutate(n_literature = scale(n_literature)[,1])

# predictors that need to be log transformed
data_regressions %>%
  select(where(is.numeric) & 
           where(~max(., na.rm = TRUE) > 1000)) %>% 
    summary()
```

### Number of records on iNaturalist per country

```{r}
#| label: rf-n_records
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

rf_n_records <- model_iNat_RF(data_df = data_regressions,
                              response_variable = 'n_records',
                              skip_vars = c('p_research_grade',
                                            'n_users',
                                            'n_species',
                                            'n_projects',
                                            'n_literature'),
                              log_vars = c('area', 
                                           'population',
                                           'gdp_per_capita',
                                           'iucn_species'))

# tuning
rf_n_records[[1]]

# observed vs predicted (test)
rf_n_records[[2]]

# observed vs predicted (CV)
rf_n_records[[3]]

# variable importance
rf_n_records[[4]]
ggsave(rf_n_records[[4]], filename='figs/variable_importance_n_records.png', device = 'png', dpi = 200, width = 8, height = 6)

# partial plots
rf_n_records[[5]]
ggsave(rf_n_records[[5]], filename='figs/partial_plots_n_records.png', device = 'png', dpi = 200, width = 8, height = 6.5)

# final model metrics rsq
rf_n_records[[6]] %>% 
  select(dataset, rsq=.estimate) %>% 
  mutate(rsq = round(rsq, 3)) %>% 
  rename(`R^2` = rsq) %>% 
  knitr::kable() %>% kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# final model metrics rmse
rf_n_records[[7]] %>% 
  select(dataset, rmse=.estimate) %>% 
  mutate(rmse = round(rmse, 3)) %>% 
  rename(`RMSE` = rmse) %>% 
  knitr::kable() %>% kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

# variable importance
rf_n_records[[9]] %>% 
  select(Variable, standardise_Importance, 
         standardise_Importance_R2) %>% 
  mutate(standardise_Importance = standardise_Importance*100) %>% 
  rename(`Importance %` = standardise_Importance,
         `Contribution to R^2` = standardise_Importance_R2) %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = c(4,1)) %>% kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

### Final numbers

```{r}
#| label: summary-performance
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

bind_rows(
  bind_rows(rf_n_records[[6]], rf_n_records[[7]]) %>% 
    mutate(response = 'n_records'),
  bind_rows(rf_n_users[[6]], rf_n_users[[7]]) %>% 
    mutate(response = 'n_users'),
  bind_rows(rf_n_species[[6]], rf_n_species[[7]]) %>% 
    mutate(response = 'n_species'),
  bind_rows(rf_n_projects[[6]], rf_n_projects[[7]]) %>% 
    mutate(response = 'n_projects'),
  bind_rows(rf_p_research_grade[[6]], rf_p_research_grade[[7]]) %>%
    mutate(response = 'p_research_grade'),
  bind_rows(rf_n_literature[[6]], rf_n_literature[[7]]) %>% 
    mutate(response = 'n_literature')
) %>% select(-.estimator) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(dataset, .metric), 
              values_from = .estimate) %>% 
  relocate(train_rmse, .after = train_rsq) %>%
  relocate(test_rmse, .after = test_rsq) %>%
  kableExtra::kbl(col.names = c('Response', 
                                'R2 train', 
                                'RMSE train',
                                'R2 test', 
                                'RMSE test',
                                'R2 CV', 
                                'RMSE CV'),
                  digits=3, format.args = list(big.mark = ',')) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_material('striped') 
```

## GLM

### Standardise predictors and outcomes

These steps are the same as for the random forests (which are done inside the function `model_iNat_RF`)

  - Log transform (`log10`) and scale predictors (mean zero).  
  - Convert `latitude` to absolute latitude.  
  - Convert `has_node` and `neighbour_has_node` to factor.

```{r}
#| label: standr-outcomes-glm
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

data_glm <- data_regressions %>% 
  mutate(area = scale(log10(area))[,1],
         population = scale(log10(population))[,1],
         gdp_per_capita = scale(log10(gdp_per_capita))[,1],
         latitude = scale(log10(abs(latitude)))[,1],
         n_species = scale(log10(n_species))[,1],
         has_node = as.factor(has_node),
         neighbour_has_node = as.factor(neighbour_has_node))

data_glm$has_node <- relevel(factor(data_glm$has_node), 
                             ref = "0")
data_glm$neighbour_has_node <- relevel(factor(data_glm$neighbour_has_node), 
                                       ref = "0")
```

### Model estimates

```{r}
#| label: lm-model-estimates
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

tidy_models <- bind_rows(
  tidy(lm_n_records, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Number of records"),
  tidy(lm_n_users, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Number of users"),
  tidy(lm_n_species, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Number of species"),
  tidy(lm_n_projects, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Number of projects"),
  tidy(lm_p_research_grade,  conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Proportion of research grade"),  
  tidy(lm_n_literature, conf.int = TRUE) %>% 
    mutate(model = "Number of publications")) %>%
  # drop intercept rows
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  # add significance markers
  mutate(
    sig_stars = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""),
    is_sig = p.value < 0.05,
    # relevel variables
    model = fct_relevel(
      model,
      "Number of records",
      "Number of users",
      "Number of species",
      "Number of projects",
      "Proportion of research grade",
      "Number of publications"),
    term = fct_relevel(
      term,
      "neighbour_has_node1",
      "has_node1",
      "latitude",
      "iucn_species",
      "gdp_in_research",
      "gdp_per_capita",
      "population",
      "area"))

tidy_models %>% 
  relocate(model) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Plot predictor importance 

```{r}
#| label: lm-predictor-importance
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-height: 14

pos <- position_dodge(1, orientation = 'y')

plot_lm_predictor_importance <- ggplot(tidy_models, 
       aes(x=term, y=estimate, 
           color=model, label=sig_stars)) +
  geom_jitter(size=2, position = pos) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Paired", name = "") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=conf.low, ymax=conf.high), width=0,
                position = pos)+
  coord_flip() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(y = "Standardised coefficient", x = NULL) +
  ggpubr::theme_cleveland() + 
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'grey99')) +
  geom_text(aes(x = term, y = estimate, 
                label = sig_stars, color = model),
            position = pos, size = 5,  
            vjust = 0.5, hjust = -0.25,  
            show.legend = FALSE)

plot_lm_predictor_importance
```

## Partial effects

```{r}
#| label: main-effects
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

effect_df <- function(model, model_name, 
                      term = "has_node", 
                      relabel = TRUE) {
  e <- effects::Effect(term, model, se = TRUE)
  df <- as.data.frame(e)
  if (relabel) {
    df[[term]] <- factor(df[[term]], levels = c("0","1"),
                         labels = c("No node","Has node"))
  }
  df$model <- model_name
  df
}

eff_list <- list(
  effect_df(lm_n_records, "Number of records"),
  effect_df(lm_n_users, "Number of users"),
  effect_df(lm_n_species, "Number of species"),
  effect_df(lm_n_projects, "Number of projects"),
  effect_df(lm_p_research_grade, "Proportion of research grade"),
  effect_df(lm_n_literature, "Number of publications"))

eff_all <- bind_rows(eff_list) %>%
  mutate(model = fct_relevel(model,
                             "Number of records",
                             "Number of users",
                             "Number of species",
                             "Number of projects",
                             "Proportion of research grade",
                             "Number of publications"))

stars_by_model <- list(
  "Number of records" = lm_n_records,
  "Number of users" = lm_n_users,
  "Number of species" = lm_n_species,
  "Number of projects" = lm_n_projects,
  "Proportion of research grade" = lm_p_research_grade,
  "Number of publications" = lm_n_literature) %>%
  imap_dfr(~ tidy(.x) %>%
             filter(grepl("^has_node", term)) %>%
             transmute(model = .y,
                       star = case_when(
                         p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
                         p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
                         p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
                         p.value < 0.1   ~ "•",
                         TRUE            ~ "")))

# join onto effect dataframe and annotate "Has node"
eff_all_star <- eff_all %>%
  left_join(stars_by_model, by = "model") %>%
  mutate(star = replace_na(star, "")) %>% 
  mutate(model = fct_relevel(
      model,
      "Number of records",
      "Number of users",
      "Number of species",
      "Number of projects",
      "Number of publications",
      "Proportion of research grade"))

pos <- position_dodge(width = 0.6)

plot_lm_main_effects <- ggplot(eff_all_star,
                               aes(x = has_node, 
                                   y = fit, color = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0,linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = pos,show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), 
                width = 0,linewidth = 1, position = pos,
                show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(eff_all_star, 
                  has_node == "Has node" & star != ""),
    aes(label = star),
    position = pos,
    hjust = -1,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 3, scales = 'fixed') +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Paired", name = "") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Partial effect") +
  ggpubr::theme_pubclean() 

plot_lm_main_effects
```
